task.name: Alias-backed price literals with no recorded provenance silently steer routing
task.story_text:
## Observed

Registry entries carry per-MTok pricing as literal values, and those literals are the sole input to
the routing cost band and to the final price tie-break among equal candidates. Some of those
entries are identified by an unversioned vendor alias, which the vendor's own tooling resolves at
invocation time to whichever concrete version it currently ships.

The result is that an entry's identity can move while its price does not, and nothing records what
the price was ever true of. The enabled `anthropic/opus/cli` entry records 15.00/75.00
(`src/theforge/config/models.py:503`) while the project's own configuration annotates the same
entry 5.00/25.00 (`forge.yaml:13`) and the runs resolve it to a concrete version billed at the
latter. Two enabled OpenAI entries diverge from their own configuration annotations the same way.

Because the figures feed banding and tie-breaking, the divergence changes selection rather than
only reporting: at the recorded values that entry bands one step more expensive than at the
charged values, and the ratio it presents against the cheap-tier entry is roughly three times the
real one.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** routing cost bands and the final price tie-break are computed from literal
  figures that do not match what the resolved model is billed at, with no indication in the record
  or the entry that they disagree.
- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/config/models.py:503` records 15.00/75.00 for an alias-identified
  entry; `forge.yaml:13` annotates the same entry with different figures; audit records show the
  alias resolving to a concrete version at invocation time, and separately show component models
  billed within the same invocation.
- **Ruled out:** not the unmeasured-cost class from #1992 and #2019 — cost is measured here and a
  figure is present, so those fixes cannot surface it.
- **Confirmed cause:** pricing is stored as an undated literal beside an identity that is not
  pinned to a version, and the only assertion covering pricing compares a registry value to the
  same registry value, so no state of the world can make the pair inconsistent.
- **Affected code path:** `config.models.custom_model_cost_rank` and
  `config.models.price_tiebreak_signal`, reading `AgentSpec.input_cost_per_mtok` and
  `output_cost_per_mtok`.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a routing input that cannot be attributed to what it describes does
  not silently participate in selection.

## Expected

A value that steers selection should be traceable to what it describes. Where a stored figure
characterises something whose identity can change without notice, the record should carry enough
provenance to tell whether the figure still applies, and a figure that cannot be attributed should
be treated as unknown rather than trusted by default. Nothing here requires a particular means of
establishing that a figure is current; the defect is that an untraceable value participates in
selection as though it were authoritative.

handoff.summary: Registry per-MTok prices are routing inputs (cost band + equal-band tie-break), and entries named by a vendor shorthand could carry a literal describing an identity that had already moved. Added pricing_provenance to AgentSpec and carried it through ModelInfo and AgentDef via a shared AttributablePricing base whose effective_input/output_cost_per_mtok collapse to None when the figures cannot be attributed. The pricing helpers moved to a new stdlib-only config/pricing.py (re-exported from models.py rather than growing the registry module): custom_model_cost_rank now takes a keyword-only pricing_provenance with no default and returns None instead of banding an untraceable literal, and price_tiebreak_signal_for(entry) is the attribution-gated signal every selection path calls — assignment.py, config/profiles.py, config/role_derivation.py, coordinator/preflight.py. config/load.py resolves the None band against RoutingPolicy.cost_rank's non-optional int via UNPRICED_COST_RANK, falling back to a declared or built-in band; operator cost: blocks and models.custom declarations are attributed to the operator's declaration. Built-in prices record the billed identity they belong to; the two Claude CLI shorthand entries deliberately do not, so their literals no longer steer selection. forge check-config names any enabled model whose price routing is ignoring.

story_deviations: Plan Step 1 said not to change routing function signatures; that constraint was incompatible with Step 3 (the plan reviewer flagged this as P1). Resolved by changing them: custom_model_cost_rank gained a keyword-only pricing_provenance with no default, and selection sites call the new price_tiebreak_signal_for(entry) rather than the two-float primitive. Every call site was migrated, so no caller keeps the old trusting behaviour by default.

The alias entries' hardcoded cost_rank literals in AGENT_REGISTRY were left as declared bands rather than re-derived from the now-ungated price — a declared band is not a figure inferred from an untraceable literal, so it is not in the defect class.

Land by hand in the main checkout if wanted.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 closes the P1: attribution now covers the cost band, not just the price tie-break. RoutingPolicy carries cost_rank_basis, and config/pricing.resolve_cost_band_basis decides it mechanically — a band equal to the entry's attributable price band is auto-attributed to that price, and any other band must name a non-price basis or construction raises. Applying that guard surfaced three built-in entries whose bands were never price-derived and had never said so: both Claude CLI shorthands (declared vendor-tier, the vendor's own tier naming, which survives the shorthand resolving to a new concrete version) and deepseek-reasoner (declared-policy, banded above its per-MTok rate because a reasoning model's token volume understates its cost at the rate alone); the unpriced Gemini previews resolve to default-unpriced automatically. config/load.py carries the same precedence for forge.yaml entries — operator declaration, this entry's attributable price, the built-in entry's own basis, then the unpriced default — so no path can reach the band of an unattributed literal. check-config prints each enabled model's band and basis. Iteration 0 (commit 2149844) remains the base: pricing_provenance on AgentSpec/ModelInfo/AgentDef, the shared AttributablePricing gate whose effective_* prices collapse to None when unattributable, price_tiebreak_signal_for at every selection site, and custom_model_cost_rank returning None instead of banding an untraceable literal.

story_deviations: anthropic/opus/cli keeps cost_rank 3 rather than being re-banded to the 2 its billed 5.00/25.00 would produce. Re-banding is actively harmful: _pick_by_tier sorts capability-desc within a band, so opus (capability 10) would lead the mid band and start winning every mid-tier role (plan/LOW, review/LOW and MEDIUM), displacing gpt-5.4. The band is instead justified on grounds independent of any price literal, which is what the spec's expected behaviour asks for.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Missing callers. price_tiebreak_signal(input, output) takes two floats, and Step 1 explicitly forbids changing routing function signatures while Step 3 requires the function to consult AgentSpec provenance. Those two constraints are mutually exclusive. The actual selection call sites are outside the plan's file list: src/theforge/assignment.py:519 and :594, src/theforge/config/profiles.py:369, src/theforge/config/role_derivation.py:260 and :320, src/theforge/coordinator/preflight.py:305, plus src/theforge/config/models.py:1011. All pass a.input_cost_per_mtok, a.output_cost_per_mtok positionally. If the dev adds an optional provenance parameter to preserve the signature, every one of those call sites keeps the old trusting behavior by default — the fix compiles, tests pass in models.py, and routing selection is unchanged. That is exactly the fix-success criterion failing.
  Suggestion: Pick one mechanism and list every file it touches: either (a) change price_tiebreak_signal to accept the AgentSpec (or an added required provenance arg) and update all seven call sites across assignment.py, profiles.py, role_derivation.py, preflight.py, models.py; or (b) expose the gating on AgentSpec itself (e.g. an effective_input_cost_per_mtok/effective_output_cost_per_mtok property that returns None when provenance is unattributable) and switch those same call sites to read the effective properties. Either way the four consumer modules belong in the plan's Files.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] custom_model_cost_rank has no 'existing unknown behavior' to return. It always returns int 1/2/3 (models.py:790-797), and its result is assigned directly into RoutingPolicy.cost_rank, which is a non-optional int (models.py:84), at src/theforge/config/load.py:277, :281, and :448. Returning None or a sentinel breaks AgentSpec construction at config load, and load.py is not in the plan's file list. Separately, the entry named in the spec — anthropic/opus/cli at models.py:503 — never calls custom_model_cost_rank: its cost_rank=3 is a hardcoded _entry argument, so gating that function has no effect on the built-in alias entry's band.
  Suggestion: State how an unattributed price is represented downstream of banding: either keep custom_model_cost_rank returning an int and handle unattributability at the AgentSpec/consumer layer, or define the unknown representation for RoutingPolicy.cost_rank and list src/theforge/config/load.py (all three call sites) as a modified file. Also say explicitly what happens to built-in entries whose cost_rank is a literal — either they get re-derived from the (now attributed) price, or the band gating applies at the consumer rather than at the constructor.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 lists Files: tests with no path. Existing coverage for this exact surface lives in tests/test_assignment_price_tiebreak.py, which asserts positional two-float calls (lines 69-96) and would need updating under either mechanism above.
  Suggestion: Name tests/test_assignment_price_tiebreak.py as a modified file and add an end-to-end assertion at a real selection site (e.g. the assignment.py:519 ranking) — a models.py-only unit test cannot prove the alias literal stopped steering selection.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The routing helpers custom_model_cost_rank and price_tiebreak_signal do not currently accept an AgentSpec instance, which makes inspecting the pricing provenance metadata difficult without signature changes. Suggestion: Add an optional spec: AgentSpec | None = None parameter to both custom_model_cost_rank and price_tiebreak_signal to allow inspecting the provenance without breaking existing callers.

Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow
